html:
A lot of the work near the I-85 corridor in Greer does not happen in a glass office tower. It happens in a spare bedroom, a converted garage, a small suite in a strip of units, or a back room behind a salon. The people who run those spaces ask us the same thing: how do you clean a place that is part home and part business? This guide is for them, and for small teams whose office is a few minutes off the interstate.

Three kinds of space we see near I-85

I-85 runs through Greer alongside SC-14, SC-101 and US-29, and it puts a mix of businesses within a short drive of GSP Airport and Downtown Greer. In our experience the spaces fall into three groups, and each one needs a slightly different plan.

Type of spaceWhat matters mostWhere we spend extra time
Home officeKeeping work areas apart from family roomsDesk surfaces, cords, shelves, the hall to the door
Small suite or studioClient-facing lookEntry glass, reception, restroom
Shared or common areasMany people, no one owns the cleanHigh-touch points, break area, trash

None of these needs a big crew. They need a clear list and someone who comes back on the same day each week.

Start with the path a client walks

When we do a walk-through, we begin at the front door and follow the route a visitor takes. If a client parks, enters, waits and uses the restroom, those four stops get the careful pass. A desk in the back can wait. This order is the same for a salon, a clinic or a home office that sees one client a week.

  • Entry mat and door glass
  • Door handles, switches and keypads
  • Waiting or reception area, dusted and wiped
  • Restroom cleaned, disinfected and restocked
  • Floors vacuumed and mopped from the farthest corner toward the door
  • Trash and recycling removed

Home offices: keeping the line between work and home

The home office is the one most people overlook. The desk gets wiped, but the keyboard edges, the monitor base, the cable tangle and the baseboard behind the chair do not. We clean those as part of a regular visit, and we do it in the same trip as the rest of the house if you also use our office cleaning in Greer service for a separate workspace.

If paperwork covers the desk, we work around it. We do not stack, sort or move documents, because it is your business and we would rather leave a pile where it is than guess. Tell us which surfaces are off limits and we mark them on the checklist.

How much does office cleaning cost near I-85?

We do not name a price until we have seen the space. The free in-home estimate is a short visit, with no commitment, where we look at the size, the restrooms, the floor types, how often you want service and what hours work. Then you get an exact price. A home office tucked into a bedroom is a different job from a two-room suite, even if both are a mile from the interstate.

To set it up, use the free estimate form, call (864) 399-5168 or text (864) 666-8520. We can usually work out a time to visit around your schedule.

Dust, pollen and traffic from the corridor

Spaces near a busy road tend to collect fine grit on sills and entry floors, and in spring the Upstate pollen settles on everything with a flat edge. We have a post on office cleaning during Upstate pollen season in Greer that explains how we adjust the checklist in those weeks. Red clay tracked in from outside is another reason entry floors get wet-mopped, not only vacuumed.

How often should it happen?

For a space with regular visitors, weekly is a common starting point. A home office with no clients can go every other week and still stay presentable. Daily service is mostly for busy retail or shared spaces with heavy restroom use. Our suggestion is to start slightly more often, then reduce once you see how the space holds up.

Perfect Services is a Brazilian-owned team, and the method we use pays attention to the edges: door frames, the track of a sliding glass door, the corner under a desk. If you want a closer look at the service, read about commercial and office cleaning. A deep cleaning before the first routine visit can also help reset a space that has not had a full clean in a while.

Small things that make a visit go well

Three habits help a small workspace stay clean between visits. Keep a bin by the entry so paper and packaging do not pile on the desk. Leave the restroom stocked, or tell us what you prefer us to restock. And clear the floor of cables, boxes and bags before we arrive, since a vacuum cannot reach under a stack. None of this is a requirement, but it lets the team spend the time on edges and corners instead of moving things.

If clients come to your home office, give them a clear route from the door to the desk and tell us about it. We will focus the careful work along that route, and treat the rest of the house as the household space it is.

If your workspace is a few minutes from I-85 and you would like a clear plan, request your free estimate for office cleaning in Greer. We will come see the space and give you a price that fits it.
faqs: Do you clean home offices, or only commercial buildings?
We clean both. A home office can be added to a regular house visit, or cleaned on its own schedule if it is a separate space used for business.
Do I need to be there during the visit?
Not always. Many clients arrange access in advance. We agree on keys or entry at the estimate and note any areas to leave alone.
How is price decided for a small workspace near I-85?
After a free in-home estimate. We look at size, restrooms, floor types and frequency, then give an exact price. We do not quote by phone or photo.
